# Generated page shape

`README.generated.md` is the narrative layer's only output. It must be derivable, line by
line, from `module.doc.json` — if a class, event or dependency isn't in the JSON, it doesn't
go in the page.

```markdown
<!-- doc:generated module=Vendor_ModuleName schema=1 -->
<!-- Generated by magento-doc-generator. Content inside these markers is regenerated
     from code. Put durable notes under "Team Notes" below. -->

# Human Readable Title

> `vendor/module-name`
> One or two sentences: what this module is for, in the reader's language.

## What it does

A short paragraph. The reason the module exists, the contracts it owns, and the boundary
it sits on. No class-by-class narration — that's the table below.

## How it works

​```
trigger → entry point
   condition
     → collaborator → external call
​```

An ASCII flow of the *main* path only. Taken from observers/plugins/cron in the JSON.

## Key components

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `Api\SomeInterface` / `Model\Some` | What it's responsible for. |

## ⚠️ Things worth knowing

- The gotchas: paths that bypass the obvious entry point, silent failure modes,
  ordering constraints, anything that has already burned someone.

<!-- doc:wiring-auto do-not-edit -->
## Wiring reference (auto-extracted)
**Observers:** `event_name` → `Observer\Class`
**Plugins:** `Target::method` ← `Plugin\Class`
**Preferences:** Interface → Implementation
Depends on: `module-a`, `magento/module-b`.
<!-- /doc:wiring-auto -->

## Related
- [[module-sibling]] · [[module-other]]
- 📄 [[runbook-something]]
<!-- /doc:generated -->

---

## Team Notes _(manual — safe from regeneration)_

_Add notes here._
```

## The markers matter

- Everything between `<!-- doc:generated -->` and `<!-- /doc:generated -->` is owned by the
  generator and replaced wholesale on every run.
- Everything after it is owned by humans and never touched.
- `apply-readme.php` stamps a `hash=` of the generated block into the opening marker. If the
  on-disk block no longer matches that hash, someone edited generated content by hand and
  the write is refused rather than silently reverting their edit.
- The `doc:wiring-auto` block is the machine-checkable part: it's rendered straight from the
  JSON, so it can be regenerated and diffed independently of the prose.

## Rules for the narrative layer

1. Never name a class, event, cron group, endpoint or dependency that isn't in the JSON.
2. Prefer the module's own vocabulary over Magento's generic one.
3. "Things worth knowing" is the highest-value section — spend the effort there.
4. If the JSON shows zero classes, say so plainly; it's a stub, not a mystery.
